subject: Edge contract extension + staged multi-vendor traffic plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: short extension + staged multi-vendor migration for Acme AI edge stack

Team —

Quick summary: Acme (our pilot customer) is up for renewal on 2026-11-01 for their managed edge/WAF/CDN contract currently with Cloudflare. Procurement has asked for a firm path that reduces single-vendor exposure and gives us pricing predictability for Q4 usage spikes.

Recommendation: negotiate a 3-month extension with Cloudflare (simple addendum) while we implement a staged traffic split (30/30/40) across Cloudflare / Fastly / Akamai for the most traffic-sensitive routes. The goal is minimal customer impact and to buy time to:
- complete the WAF rule parity work
- validate origin shield and cache-hit rates across vendors
- finalize long-term economics and preferred vendor for 2027

I've attached: SOW_edge_transition_draft_v3.pdf (drafted with Solutions), cost_comparison_20261008.xlsx (est. egress and per-TB), and traffic-shift-runbook.md (technical steps + rollback).

Open questions I want us to surface in internal review:
1) SLA floor we will accept for the extension (Cloudflare offering 99.9% vs our target 99.95).
2) Whether finance will approve a short-term uplift to committed TB for Q4 to lock in price caps.
3) Security sign-off: Marcus, we need a statement that WAF parity + logging (audit logs, raw request capture retention) meets Acme's SOC2 evidence needs.

Next steps: please review attachments and reply with redlines/concerns by EOD Friday (Oct 8). If we align, I'll ask Connor for a 90-day addendum and a capped overage rate.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: SOW_edge_transition_draft_v3.pdf (pdf), cost_comparison_20261008.xlsx (spreadsheet), traffic-shift-runbook.md (text)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: short extension + staged multi-vendor migration for Acme AI edge stack

Karthik —

Thanks for the packet. High level from Procurement/Finance:
- 90-day extension is preferable to avoid a hard break; legal will push for minimal term/auto-expire language.
- We can float an additional $15k for Q4 committed egress to secure better per-TB pricing, but need a firm forecast from Acme (weekly burn rate) before committing.
- If Cloudflare can include a 10% credit for unplanned DDoS mitigation over the 90-day window, Finance is likely to accept the extension.

Action items for us:
- Laura, can you confirm whether legal prefers an SOW amendment or a new addendum template?
- Marcus, any immediate red flags on the cost comparison? I see Fastly looks cheaper at scale but has higher on-demand overage.

I added comments to cost_comparison_20261008.xlsx (sheet: finance_notes).

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Strategic Procurement
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment references: cost_comparison_20261008.xlsx (comments added)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: short extension + staged multi-vendor migration for Acme AI edge stack

Karthik / team —

Security perspective: overall OK provided we do the following before flipping traffic:
- WAF rule parity test harness (see traffic-shift-runbook.md: section 2.3). We must validate identical block/allow behavior for the top 25 signatures Acme relies on.
- Centralized logging: ensure we can collect raw request logs from Fastly & Akamai in the same format we get from Cloudflare (preferably via our ELK ingestion pipeline).
- Retention SLA: Acme requires 90 days of raw request logs for audit; confirm vendors for log retention and egress pricing.

I also forwarded a short note from Cloudflare's account rep that clarifies their extension terms. See below.

-----Original Message-----
From: Connor Hale <connor.hale@cloudflare.com>
Sent: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 14:12:00 -0700
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Subject: Cloudflare short-term extension details

Marcus —
Per our call: we can offer a 90-day addendum that keeps current committed iTB levels, includes a 10% credit for DDoS mitigation events tied to a threshold, and locks uplift overage to $35/TB for Q4. We can also share access to raw logs for 90 days; extended retention will be a separate line item. I can send an addendum + DocuSign link if you authorize.

Connor Hale
Senior Account Executive, Cloudflare
connor.hale@cloudflare.com
-----

Marcus

P.S. We should scope a short smoke test for the top 3 Acme endpoints before any 30/30/40 split. That will catch most parity issues quickly.

Marcus Lin
Security Lead, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Connor Hale <connor.hale@cloudflare.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: short extension + staged multi-vendor migration for Acme AI edge stack

Hi Karthik / team —

Thanks for outlining the path. To recap the offer we can fast-track:
1) 90-day addendum, same committed throughput, auto-expire on 2027-01-01.
2) $35/TB capped overage for Q4.
3) 10% DDoS mitigation credit tied to mitigation events documented by our SOC.
4) Raw request log access for 90 days (S3-compatible export). Longer retention priced separately.

DocuSign link (addendum): https://docusign.example.com/CF-addendum-Acme-90d (expires in 7 days)
Runbook stub (read-only): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-edge-runbook

If you accept, we'll prepare the addendum and can run a smoke test environment the week of Oct 18.

Connor Hale
Senior Account Executive
Cloudflare
connor.hale@cloudflare.com

Attachments: addendum_summary.pdf (summary of terms)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor Hale <connor.hale@cloudflare.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: short extension + staged multi-vendor migration for Acme AI edge stack

All —

Thank you, everyone — clear alignment from Procurement and Security. Plan of record:
1) Approve Cloudflare 90-day addendum as Connor outlined. Marissa, please confirm finance approval of the $15k Q4 buffer and sign off on the DocuSign link.
2) Marcus to run WAF parity smoke tests for top 3 endpoints the week of Oct 18; traffic-shift-runbook.md is the playbook; runbook owner: Marcus.
3) Solutions + Infra will begin configuration with Fastly & Akamai for origin shield and log exports in parallel. Target split: 30% Cloudflare / 30% Fastly / 40% Akamai for non-authenticated static content (auth flows remain on Cloudflare until full parity).
4) Legal (cc'd) — please review the addendum template and confirm we can accept auto-expire language w/o rolling obligations.

Connor — please go ahead and send the DocuSign for the 90-day addendum; we'll aim to have procurement sign within 48 hours of receipt. Once signed, infra will schedule the smoke tests.

I'll update Acme's procurement contact once signed and copy this thread.

Karthik
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Next steps checklist: sign addendum, fund Q4 buffer, run smoke tests (Oct 18-22), start rolling traffic split on Oct 25.
